title: EVENT RECAP: SIGGRAPH Asia 2024 in Tokyo
content:
_This year, Siggraph Asia has been a fulfilling experience, a precious time to connect_

 _with developers, students, researchers, and our belated Marvelous Designer users._

_Thank you once again for visiting our booth and sharing your valuable experiences with us!_

_Here is a quick recap of the event in Tokyo._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e00196b539a542259d5e120208493cae/images/d2d5d254be81460d93f16125cf7c8fc8a6e83d6a649e421f8e8fe4e824436562.jpg)

At this Siggraph, we wanted to support and cater to everyone who wanted to get to know the marvelous designer, whether they had known us before or not.

So, our in-house designers held a talk session at the booth covering Japanese garment making and introducing new features in both English and Japanese.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e00196b539a542259d5e120208493cae/images/756189a8904c4a8887954c3ff98065556794b3cf9ff0483e946ea43ac6ca9e53.jpg)

Marvelous Designer is best known not only for the realistic simulation but also for the low learning curve.

At one side of the station, we had a game booth for the 'Tying Knot Challenge'. Allow every participant to experience how easy it is for them to create the garment. And the winner who tied the knot the fastest had made less than 40 seconds. Nailed it!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e00196b539a542259d5e120208493cae/images/b456c38ae0df47c4b49c53138d47831353fd97c6a6ee4f23995bb02a93d67cfb.jpg)

Additionally, we had a very special demo station for the participants.

We offered personalized demo stations with three of our Marvelous Designers' in-house designers in three different languages, Japanese, Chinese and Korean, for any participant to ask questions freely. We hope you have a chance to connect with our most insightful designers for any questions you may have about Marvelous Designer!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e00196b539a542259d5e120208493cae/images/5a7c5523447a463d80bd8cabd3721864d82aad5ce8234e6fa988c8f08b96b293.jpg)

Even if you did not have a chance to stop by but need help with the design, that's okay.

In 2025 we will have the Marvelous Designer forum back with us!

This will help connect you with not only our in-house designers but also with the strong community of Marvelous Designer users. Stay tuned for more.

Out of all the great moments, the most memorable ones are when people come up and say 'I've been using Marvelous Designer and it has been making my life much easier.' It was always a pleasure to reconnect with our belated users and listen to their great experiences.

This is definitely what makes our team thrive. We, the Marvelous Designer team, will continue to value your insights and be part of your design journey.

Thank you so much for the stop by and we look forward to bonding with you at the next event.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e00196b539a542259d5e120208493cae/images/467f1c6d45db4e95899f77c070648a79aa7a034a89eb4f0f8c1951ca58dcd783.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e00196b539a542259d5e120208493cae/images/218f6f6295764afe92f0b9728fb17b31Img%20frame%20%282%29.png)

Reply 1: The upcoming events will be posted in the notice, so make sure to check it out regularly! 😊

title: Marvelous Designer 2024.2 is HERE!
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/3e260cf8818a4ebf8d0639f1c610ab79/images/84976d5696ab42d283677cff20d71be003a61cce503247f7860fb1ee92e57b15.png)

## _We’d like to share exciting new updates in 2024.2,_

## _with key improvements in simulation, interoperability, and more._

* * *

The highlight of the new version is Marvelous Designer’s **_enhanced GPU simulation_** —which **now matches the accuracy of CPU simulation** and can even be used for Animation Caching. GPU simulation brings significant speed improvements compared to CPU simulation, and now, after improvements from the team at CLO Virtual Fashion, the quality of the simulation is also on par. It dramatically accelerates design processes by allowing faster pattern creation and simulation in the 3D window. Artists can seamlessly switch between the faster GPU simulation and the stable, trusted CPU simulation from previous versions.

Another major improvement is a **_trim simulation with improved collision accuracy_**. This allows **artists to have greater control over collision properties such as weight and stiffness, boosting the realism of garments beyond perfect wrinkles**. The update amplifies the level of detail artists can achieve in their simulations through trims.

**_The advanced pinching with soft selection feature_** also offers greater control than ever before. Unlike previous versions, which limited selection to a single vertex, **artists can now use the customizable soft selection tool to select garments with smooth falloff shapes during simulation.** This adds precision and flexibility when fine-tuning details or fixing intersecting patterns, offering significantly more control compared to past versions.

On the interoperability front, the **_GoZ Plugin_** has been improved with the **latest versions of Marvelous Designer and ZBrush** , adding more options that grant artists greater flexibility and control. [(ZBrush Download)](https://www.maxon.net/en/downloads)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/3e260cf8818a4ebf8d0639f1c610ab79/images/dfdd7630f5614365a655b58d73032b9c3fcd06755bc940fea6ad28b8fd38b836.png)

Lastly, Marvelous Designer 2024.2 brings significant enhancements to **_automatic quad remeshing_** _,_**delivering cleaner topology with faster, more efficient post-processing cleanup**. The new update emphasizes the reduction of irregular meshes and an increase in overall quadrangulation quality regarding mesh flow and structure. Previously, achieving the desired topology required a degree of manual adjustment. With this latest improvement, along with recent features focused on retopology, artists now have the tools needed within Marvelous Designer to set the proper quad mesh distribution for their designs.

  


# Overall, Marvelous Designer 2024.2 delivers key upgrades to __**_speed_** _,_**_accuracy_** _, and_** _integration_** _,_ ensuring a smoother and more powerful user experience than ever before. We hope our new updates will increase your work efficiency.  
  
[**[****SEE ALL FEATURES****]**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/learn/newfeature?v=2024.2)  
  
Thanks for your support! 

  


If you have any questions, please feel free to [**contact us**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact)! 

Marvelous Designer Team 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/3e260cf8818a4ebf8d0639f1c610ab79/images/34bb7396eff444b7b2f3804fbfc6bf3dSocial%20Media%20Release%202024.2.png)

title: The Bandit of Solis Tomb
content:
## _Let's chase a classic bounty hunter storyline inspired by "Cowboy Bebop: The Movie." An amazing character-creation story awaits!_

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/db0b4d1dc5184ab9b9f076f693cb53efezgif-1-3ce3b395f2.webp)

# **Interview with Daire Powell | The Bandit of Solis Tomb﻿ | Artist &Film-maker**

* * *

# **Can you start by introducing yourself and sharing a bit about your background?**

My name is Daire Powell and I am a 23 year old Artist/Film-maker from Ireland. I recently graduated from the National College of Art and Design in Dublin with a BA in Moving Image Design. From a young age I have always been interested in film and animation, firstly experimenting with stop-motion animation using home made rigs and as I got older, cinematic video editing within games and 3D. My passions began with more traditional roots, putting a lot of my time into more fine art practices such as sketching and painting. However as I got older and leaned into digital media, I learned that I could blend my traditional backgrounds with newer forms of media to find a balanced workflow that benefits me. Originally I went to university to focus on live-action filming techniques but soon rediscovered my love for animation and bringing my own worlds to life. During the last two to three years of my course I dived heavily into using Blender and other traditional methods of animation, eventually developing my first original short film "The Friend, The Dove & The Deer" which managed to make it to a few festivals in Ireland and Canada. I am currently working as a freelancer in the games and esports community as well as developing personal animated films in my free time. You can find more information about me and my work on my [Website](https://dairemovesthings.cargo.site/).

# **What was the story or concept behind your artwork for the Kinetic Rush challenge? How did the idea come to life?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/440ef0a087a740ff9c5a3cad7e4c03d1Copy_of_title%20%281%29.webp)

"The Bandit of Solis Tomb" is a short piece based on a frog-bandit; a wanted criminal in a small desert town after the disappearance of an ancient relic from Solis Tomb. He is on the run from the A.P.U (Automatic Police Unit) whilst hiding out in the local markets. I was inspired by the portrayal of the eastern style markets in “Cowboy Bebop: The Movie” and have always loved a classic bounty hunter storyline.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/529adf32f78642aea7183c296239e053Copy_of_ref1.webp)

Finding those nooks and crannies between locations is something I love in world building and was an important influence for the setting of this piece. I often take strong inspiration from old storybooks or the stereotypes around them and enjoy playing with those ideas, that is why I decided to use a frog with humanoid proportions and movements to reference old fairy tale tropes. The style of the animation and shading is something I have been developing and experimenting with for a while now since my first short film. This project was a sort of test run for the processes to be used in my future works.

# **It's very interesting that you used Marvelous Designer for 2D animation. What inspired you to use Marvelous Designer for this project, and how did it help you achieve your artistic vision?**

Generally in stylised forms of animation, it's more common to include the clothing in your rig to have more control over cloth as a character in itself. However, I thought the juxtaposition between using a 2D-stylised character and physical based cloth simulations could work well and, with this movement being primarily at speed, help sell my secondary action with the detail that Marvelous can provide me. I have used the Blender cloth simulator for a few years now and understand how tough it can be sometimes, especially with complex characters and animation, to successfully execute the right simulation without third party addons. Marvelous Designer gives me a more real time simulation workflow with good quality that allows me to "trial and error" my clothing until it flows the way that I want as a sequence.

# **Could you walk us through the tools you used in your workflow? How did Marvelous Designer fit into your pipeline?**

The tools that I mainly used in my workflow are Blender, Substance Painter, Rebelle 7, Marvelous Designer and After Effects. I would say that my workflow for this piece from a 3D standpoint was pretty standard, but when it came to texturing and cloth, there were a few more steps to be taken to achieve the look that I wanted. In the Kinetic Rush challenge we were tasked with creating a scene and a story from scratch, being given only a base animation to use. I started by blocking out my scene in Blender with simple shapes and retargeting the animation to a custom character that I modelled. Once I had my composition and my character cleaned up, I was ready for my texturing and simulation process.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/c7ffc557762848c19a3a895741dcd497Copy_of_ref2.webp)

When it comes to texturing, I like to be pretty hands on with the freedom to be messy and create manual texture and shapes. For the characters I used Substance Painter to paint a flat base texture that will eventually be put back into Blender to drive my stylized shader.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/3be286e7d5cd4374a842d07fd593464eCopy_of_ref3.webp)

For background elements, scene texturing and animation sprites I used Rebelle 7 which is what gives my work a tactile impression. I created a collection of base textures to use and some more element specific ones to layer on top in the shader. Every single texture in this artwork was painted by hand, with time saving methods of reuse and combinations of paintings.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/7e54f90639834b14b293349201c37506886e3cbbc79841af9335e8a339d8fc5f.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/a22a707bd5d9411bbf6efad496c42a6be24d0edbfe5d4864989129b323fc9c67.webp)

I needed to find a way to fit Marvelous Designer into this workflow in both character design and texturing. Marvelous has a great library of garments that you can purchase from the store which really helped with my lack of fashion design knowledge and with the short timeframe that we had to create the project. I purchased two pieces of clothing that helped give a lot of personality and culture to my character. The garments were quite loose and simple in design so fitting it to my non-human character wasn’t difficult, I just moved the 3D pattern to fit around my character and GPU simulated it until it was in a natural position. Marvelous Designers layering system is also a great tool that helped me differentiate the folds in his hood and wasteline.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/8c0724b5f31d408c8e0f014ff705dd35Copy_of_ref6.webp)

The relation between the 2D pattern window in Marvelous and exported UVs came in very handy for my texture workflow. I was able to export a clean unfolded version of my garment that I could bring into Rebelle for manually painting my details.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/d31e34be9fe1418f95da101a0258cb67Copy_of_ref7.webp)

Being able to export in stable animation data formats such as alembic has helped me convert my 3D simulations into a frame-by-frame look. Blender allows us to manually override the frames being used from an alembic so all I had to do was import the garment and step the simulation frames to time with my 12 FPS character.

As mentioned before, I wanted my clothing to juxtapose my character in realism so I used layered passes in the compositing stage so that I could render my cloth with Cycles and a holdout in Blender while keeping my character in Eevee. This created the 2D/3D combination that I needed. More behind the scenes can be found in my short Breakdown Video.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/148fb6441a8845e8a3032585ca3f7343Copy_of_ref8.webp)

On that note, I have since been exploring more ways to use Marvelous Designer in a "2D-shaded" 3D pipeline. Recently I have been experimenting with manually painting normals in Substance for an upcoming film. I needed a way that I could blend this method with my clothing; considering that there can be many tight folds when simulating animations. I realised that if I export the T pose of my Marvelous simulation and bring it into Substance Painter, I can use that frame as a base normal to add my painted averages before my simulation creates folds that are hard to paint.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1eb2fb8ddc8b4746a09776150aafcd41/images/564c2f4e30fb44cf979135c13ae93b5cCopy_of_ref9.webp)

# **Are there any standout moments, scenes, or characters in your project that Marvelous Designer was especially useful for?**

I used Marvelous Designer for my main character's costume and also an easter-egg character in the background that will appear in a later work coming soon on YouTube. Marvelous came in handy for any complex animations that needed to interact with fabric.

# **What were some of the challenges you faced during the project, and how did you overcome them?**

My main challenge on this project was honestly just painting everything, manual processes are something that I hold dearly in my heart and they should always be practised, but they are very time consuming. My compromise was to create a range of general textures that I could use as texture brushes or masks in the shader editor in Blender. That way I could keep layering with diversity without painting every single stroke again.

Another challenge would have been the clothing design but I was lucky that the Marvelous store had a vast selection and exactly what I was looking for. With more time and experience, I am hoping to dive deeper into creating beautiful garments like these from scratch in Marvelous.

# **Do you have any tips or advice for other 3D artists looking to incorporate Marvelous Designer into their workflow?**

Don't be afraid to break the rules a bit and play! 3D simulation is a very technical process and hard to jump into, you might also expect to do things in a set way, but within a software like Marvelous Designer there is so much potential to find your own workflow to suit your needs - From realistic to stylised. Just play with simple garments first and the rest will come to you over time.

# **Finally, how would you describe your overall experience using Marvelous Designer on this project?**

Overall I had a great time using Marvelous for this piece and will definitely be referring to it again when it comes to character costume in animation. It definitely has its frustrating moments, like any 3D simulation software does, but the speed and detail that it can simulate cloth in comparison to other 3D softwares i've used feels unmatched so far. Having found a workflow where I only need to fit a character once and just click simulate for each action, has been extremely beneficial to my artistic journey.
content_description: Explore the captivating world of bounty hunting through character creation and artistic innovation inspired by "Cowboy Bebop: The Movie" in Daire Powell's interview and project showcase.

title: Ranchero (Bounty Hunter)
content:
## _Alex Savelev's Ranchero (Bounty Hunter) project showcases his mastery in creating hyper-realistic fabric folds using Marvelous Designer. From intricate poncho folds to seamless fabric simulation, every detail brings the character to life._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/77df16324d97477a9c9ff5422b12e545random%200.jpg)

# **Interview with Alex Savelev |**[**Ranchero (Bounty Hunter)﻿**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/x3DExE)**| 3D Character Artist**

* * *

# **Could you please introduce yourself to the Marvelous Designer community members?**

My name is Alex. I spent most of my career working in graphic design and advertising. My journey as a 3D artist began when I watched the cinematics of Death Stranding in 2018. I was so impressed that when the pandemic hit, I quit my job and moved to my country house. There, working alone for 12 hours a day, I managed to get a job as a character 3D artist after two years.

# **Tell us about the project. What inspired you? Is there a particular story or setting behind it?**

The robot creation project inspired me with the opportunity to combine soft, flexible materials like fabric and ropes with hard elements — rusty metal and plastic, which the robot itself is made of. This blend of textures, along with the fusion of Mexican Western and sci-fi themes, brought a unique vibe to the concept.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/a9db09dc7ab045298214f2e196b887baquestion_2.jpg)

# **How did Marvelous Designer contribute to your creative process? Are there any particular processes you'd like to highlight for our community members?**

One of the key elements of the concept was the Mexican poncho. To make it realistic, I needed to create believable folds that would reflect the weight and density of the fabric, along with its worn look. Usually, I use Marvelous Designer for creating complex clothing patterns, but here the pattern was quite simple, so I focused on the folds. During the process, I used pins, adjusted gravity settings (which is very useful for simulating heavy fabrics), changed the fabric's friction settings, and tried out the sculpting tools for the first time, which were introduced relatively recently. After setting all the necessary parameters, I was able to achieve the desired result quickly. My advice is to set up all the parameters initially before starting the simulation.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/6603e55fe03e4c3ca1696f81ca7b3bfeUV.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/ec26dbf798814cc0b86dfc3c90b52792cool_folds.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/6127c22ec3184473bbe680e37228f272marvv_gravity.png)

# **The textures and details on the shawl are very intricate. How did you use Marvelous Designer to achieve such a worn, realistic look?**

To achieve the worn effect, I created three fabric bases in Marvelous: one exported as a quad (grid) and the other as a triangle (which I then retopologized). I often use Quad (grid) if I plan to apply special effects in ZBrush, as the even polygons, aligned with the fabric, allow for creating stunning textures using the MicroPoly tool. This is how I created the thick threads that are clearly visible on the neck. Combined with compression folds, they look very realistic. I used the other fabric layer to create worn, damaged areas. This gave me three fabric layers with different textures, which I alternated to create the look of worn-out fabric or leave it intact.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/4457526bb47740b5be5ac67997fa4e65question_4_1.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/a2f0299c417949048b603a75fc31fbc5question_4.jpg)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

In my work, I use the standard tools in Marvelous Designer and recently started using sculpting, which has been very satisfying. I often work with the "steamer" tool to get the exact folds I need. Additionally, I frequently use pins, manually crafting custom folds. Before running the simulation, I increase the mesh density and remove all the pins to avoid leaving any marks on the fabric. Although high-density mesh simulation runs slowly, this helps retain the original shape of my pinned folds.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/4f01f8c11a7a4ac39109033c9fc481edquestion_5.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/207b6d7781f34584bff54ae7d412f94asculpting.png)

# **What challenges did you face during the creation process, and how did you overcome them?**

Sometimes, it's hard to stop when working on clothing simulation. I can spend hours on this process, creating increasingly expressive folds. The process is incredibly captivating, and it's essential to know when to stop. 😊

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you want to share with the community?**

As a 3D character artist, I appreciate Marvelous not only for its ability to create incredibly realistic fabrics but also for its help with retopology. I often use Mesh (Grid) to create a base for retopologizing objects, which saves a lot of time. This mesh type is also perfect for creating items like cloaks, where there are hardly any seams, eliminating the need to triangulate the mesh.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b26dbf262d5d4373bf4f381331582eaa/images/1b3e5b897e4044978c32a7d55d3ffadequestion_7.jpg)

# **How would you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

I've been using Marvelous for four years now, and in that time, I've completed numerous personal and commercial projects. I've created a vast array of clothing models and love this tool for helping my characters look truly alive. Moreover, I've become a genuine fan of creating different types of folds — something I never imagined was possible!

# **by  Alex Savelev**  
[** _Artstation_**](https://www.artstation.com/alexsavelev)

## _Meet Manuel Peter, a winner of the "Marvelous" award from the Kinetic Rush 3D Community Challenge._

* * *

# **Interview with Manuel Peter |**[**Japanese Battlefield**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/lGRzKa)**| 3D Generalist**

* * *

# ** _Congratulations on winning the "Marvelous" award in the_**[** _Kinetic Rush 3D community challenge!_**](https://kineticrush.createwithclint.com/)

* * *

# **Can you start by introducing yourself and sharing a bit about your background?**

My name is Manuel Peter and I am a 3D Generalist from Germany. I have around 14 years of experience in 3D, and have worked with a lot of different 3D Software (including C4D, Max, and others), but my main tool is blender. I work part time in a publicity agency doing 3D animations and product visualizations for industry companies. I am also freelancing and doing private 3D projects, for example the PWNISHER challenges. I was among the top 5 in the BOSSFIGHT challenge, as well as in the ETERNAL ASCENT challenge. In the most recent KINETIC RUSH challenge I got into the top 100. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7194a045d1ab4817805e51a9c79d2b68/images/6f0b47416bb04ea0a7489dcf67fd9f24Manuel%206.JPG)

# **We'd love to hear more about your winning piece. What was the story or concept behind your artwork for the Kinetic Rush challenge? How did the idea come to life?**

When a challenge starts and the topic is released I usually give myself a day or two to think about possible ideas that would work within the template file. After that I start collecting references and gather them inside of pureref. The idea that seemed the most promising to me, was a clash of two armies, heavily inspired by the ride of the Rohirrim in Lord of the rings, as well as the battle of bastards in Game of Thrones. My main website for references is pinterest and somehow I also ended up with a lot of images of Japanese clothing and Japanese landscapes, which was at first a separate idea for an animation. 

Pondering which of my two ideas to pick, I finally came up with the idea of mixing both. Taking the general battle setup from the first idea, mixing it with the aesthetics and setting of the second idea. Knowing that this would be a massive amount of work, not knowing if the outcome would be cinematic as I imagined it in my head, I was a little bit hesitant if I could realize a project that big in that short time period. Gathering a lot of kimono style references I was sure that I wanted a female main character, separating her from the rest of the people involved in the battle. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7194a045d1ab4817805e51a9c79d2b68/images/233a23edd2544e39bddaeecbf8cb191cManuel%202.png)

# **What inspired you to use Marvelous Designer for this project, and how did it help you achieve your artistic vision?**  

I worked with Marvelous Designer some years ago and I was thrilled when I heard the MD is joining the Challenge with a free month. So I immediately downloaded it, as I was sure to use it for the cloth simulation. As the motion within the template file was really fast, I knew that it would be challenging to get a consistent and realistic cloth movement, without crashing the simulation. As MD has more advanced settings and tools than blender's internal cloth simulation, I was sure that MD was my only choice to get what I had visualized.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7194a045d1ab4817805e51a9c79d2b68/images/274faab356e840768f17f7ca19d0836bkinetic_rush_MD_01-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)

# **Could you walk us through the tools you used in your workflow? How did Marvelous Designer fit into your pipeline?**  

As the idea was clear I immediately started blocking out a basic 3D scene with the template file. I kitbashed some models in there and also did a quick lighting setup. 

I usually do this step in my projects, to see if I can get an aesthetic looking image, mainly focusing on the general scene setup and the lighting. If the result is somewhat pleasing I continue my work (motivated by the first test renders). If I don't come to a satisfying result I would stop working on that idea. 

Seeing my first test I was a little bit more secure I could end up with a nice animation. So at this point I started my work on the female main character. I started with a female base mesh from Blender Market. I edited the mesh to get a more Asian looking character (sculpting in a blender), worked on the hair and the textures. 

Retargeting the animation data from the template and adapting the rig for animation were the next steps. After that I didn't lose any time and got straight into the animation of the character. The sword strike and the jump were custom animations, partly with motion capture data from mixamo and partly hand animated. 

In Marvelous Designer, I imported a clean A pose of the female. I searched the store for a basic kimono and downloaded it. I changed all the patterns and the sewing, adapting it to my character, added more cloth parts like belts and other cloth parts. This got me quite close to my reference images. After I was satisfied with the cloth (there was quite some back and forth there) I started with the simulation. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7194a045d1ab4817805e51a9c79d2b68/images/a384b25f0044452aa6d61efb5e3fcee1Manuel%207.JPG)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7194a045d1ab4817805e51a9c79d2b68/images/e3b4fbc586754c4eaf0fff0ecab46acbManuel%209.JPG)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7194a045d1ab4817805e51a9c79d2b68/images/1196e21e205e498c8c0fd3a0c1ba18a0Manuel%208.JPG)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7194a045d1ab4817805e51a9c79d2b68/images/078df7f90fa7428c88a099a411bb3199Manuel%205.JPG)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7194a045d1ab4817805e51a9c79d2b68/images/9c4c6140bd9f4059875559eed8d39149Manuel%201.JPG)

# **Are there any standout moments, scenes, or characters in your project that Marvelous Designer was especially useful for?**

Realistically speaking, the project, and especially the main character, would not be feasible without Marvelous Designer. The fast and harsh movements, paired with my wish for a super realistic cloth simulation, made it clear that my only chance would be Marvelous Designer, as you can iterate quickly at a high speed. Not having to wait minutes or hours for the baking of the simulation, was a lifesaver. With my GTX4090 the performance in MD was awesome. 

# **What were some of the challenges you faced during the project, and how did you overcome them?**

As the movement was very fast and there were a lot of abrupt changes in direction it was pretty hard to get a pleasing result. Oftentimes the character lost the cloth while simulating due to the fast movements of the character. Other times the arm animation pushed away the lower parts of the kimono. So there was a lot of testing of different cloth types and physics settings. With the help of pining groups I overcame these issues and finally got a usable, realistic cloth simulation. Because I reworked the animation in blender about 10 times, I also had to re simulate it every time in marvelous designer, which was quite time consuming. But thanks to the fast simulation in Marvelous Designer it was doable. 

#  **Do you have any tips or advice for other 3D generalists looking to incorporate Marvelous Designer into their workflow?**

Just try it out. If you are looking for a versatile, fast tool that delivers realistic cloth simulations, Marvelous Designer is the only choice in my opinion. I worked quite a lot with Blender's cloth simulation system in the past, and I also did some smaller simulation in this project like flags etc. with Blender, which worked fine. But if it comes to high poly simulation on complex animations, blender surely comes to a limit. In these situations Marvelous Designer shines. Also the switch between blender and Marvelous Designer with alembic files was no problem at all and worked fast and without any errors. 

# **Finally, how would you describe your overall experience using Marvelous Designer on this project?**

It was an awesome experience. And I can't wait to do more work with Marvelous Designer, also for more experimental or abstract animations, and further work on combining blender and MD. As much as I love blender, you should always be open to trying other software, especially if these software do specific tasks on a higher level. Best examples are Marvelous Designer, but also software like embergen and LiquiGen.

# **by  Manuel Peter**

title: Tuxingsun - A Fusion of Inspiration and Chinese Lore
content:
## _Artist Mendy BM reimagines Tuxingsun from Investiture of the Gods with Marvelous Designer, bringing every stitch and detail of the costume to life._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/94e2c64fffd44e43bae3e53e056e16e2Tx_mendy-bm-skin-color.jpg)

# **Interview with Mendy BM |**[**Tuxingsun**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/V28Jk8)**﻿ | Game Character Artist**

* * *

# **Could you please introduce yourself to the Marvelous Designer community members?**

Hi everyone! I'm Mendy BM, game character artist from Brasil, based in Spain. I started my professional career creating modular digital humans for medical learning, and since 2022, I've been working in the game industry, creating fantasy characters and creatures for games.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/c150fb25bbe144929c0d906351c131fe1_mendy-bm-Dark-Elf.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/e3413a1a2205468aa386c517f4e6fad01_mendy-bm-mendybm-ecorche.jpg)

# **Please tell us about the project. What inspired you to choose Tuxingsun from the Chinese literature I _nvestiture of the Gods_ as your project?**

Since the beginning of my career, I've been following [Xu Tianhua](https://www.artstation.com/tianhuaxu) and [Yang Qi](https://www.artstation.com/yangqi917). Their work is a great inspiration for me. "Tuxingsun" concept made by Xu Tianhua, always caught my attention with his little body and unique face features. At the research stage, to know more about the backstory of the character, I found John Zhu's Chinese Lore Podcast, where he retells classic Chinese literature in English, and I fell in love with it. China has a millenary culture, which has many of the biggest inventions in the humankind history, and I'm very interested to know more, especially about their art.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/2d3da966582b434784dd157086d20d2f1_mendy-bm-Tuxingsun.jpg)

# **How did Marvelous Designer assist you in realizing the vision for Tuxingsun's costume? Did you use any specific features or techniques that helped bring authenticity to the fabric and clothing design?**

I started the Tuxingsun project to familiarize myself with Marvelous Designer and I found incredible the possibility to work with sewing patterns, like is done in real-life cloth industry. Also, being able to work on the 2D pattern window and see the changes in real time, at the 3D window, is something extremely handy and powerful for recreating cloth designs. Additionally, there are a great number of fabric presets available, experimenting with it is so important to bring authenticity to the fabric, as well as finding the right pattern for it.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/152355aa363e4e66b69ef467e385827cTx_mendy-bm-camisa2.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/aa8be76704134d2b83b764b1fa19a134Tx_mendy-bm-pano1.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/8014037f03ee4f9db2e546bbb932a485Tx_mendy-bm-front.jpg)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

When I start a project, I spend a good amount of time finding good references, then, I use PureRef to make the reference board, selecting just a few images on each topic.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/aa7777cfe41e41869d56b0a7041ec0a84_PureRef_Tuxingsun.jpg)

After that, I go to Zbrush, to sculpt the character's and prop's basic shapes, with all my attention on proportions and silhouette. On personal projects, at this stage, I make pauses every now and then, to rest the eyes and be able to see clearer the results I'm getting, furthermore I often use Krita to make "correction" drawings on screenshots of Zbrush.

Once I got a result I'm happy with, I moved forward to create the garments at Marvelous Design, taking advantage of its incredible cloth simulation power. After that I returned to Zbrush, and created the high poly version of everything, refined some folds and added all the details.

Following, I used 3D Max to create the low poly version of the character and then imported it on RizomUV to work on the UVs. Finally, on Adobe Substance Painter, imported the lowpoly, and did the bakes and textures for the whole character. 

For rendering and final testing, I tend to use Marmoset Toolbag and Unreal 5.

# **What challenges did you face during the creation process, and how did you overcome them?**

For me it was the number of layers, making the garment without the pieces intersecting with each other was complicated and the "freeze" tool was very important to overcome this challenge. I had to freeze and unfreeze the cloth elements many times, going back and forward, activating the simulation to create the folds that I wanted, and simultaneously, trying to maintain the elements hierarchy.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/d2786d02057c4077b7888f4f1663f2d55_Tuxingsun_steps.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/21c4cbc7118945b1919b48da2a28a50f5_marvelous_capture2.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/fdd29bc8a6c1444983e819de713f3f625_marvelous_capture1.JPG)

Also, when I created the patterns, the cloth was small on Tuxingsun's body. Because of that, I had to "add more fabric" and this broke the hierarchy. So to avoid this, when I started over, I used a high particle distance to get the shapes, then I changed to a lower value and used many pins to simulate it and create the desired folds again.

In summary, to maintain the hierarchy, the freeze and unfreeze features, in conjunction with the pins, were my best friends in this project. This was the most time-consuming part of the work.

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

The first tip: take your time to find patterns, this will save you a lot of time. Even though it's difficult and frustrating to find patterns on the internet, humans have started to create garments since ancient times; take the time to find them. Second tip: don't forget to use symmetry. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1f7f0a3eddcf49d0bf364a01d959c66e/images/35f034d2d9f14fbbb097bc6ee02364be6_Tuxingsun%20process_translucent.jpg)

Third: when you have as many pins as I had, the translucent mode is very useful. In addition, more a feature than a trick, use the soft body simulation, it's an incredible feature that considers the elastic aspect of the skin.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

It's amazing, the software is very intuitive, and the interface is truly user-friendly. Nowadays it is the best software option to create 3D garments in the industry.

# **by  ****Mendy BM**  
[** _Artstation_**](https://www.artstation.com/mendybm)
content_description: Explore the creative journey of artist Mendy BM as he brings the character Tuxingsun from *Investiture of the Gods* to life through stunning costume design using Marvelous Designer.

title: MARVELOUS DESIGNER IN CFX
content:
## _Explore Diego Conte's creative journey behind The Witness for Love, Death & Robots and the Oscar-winning short film The Windshield Wiper!_

* * *

# **Interview with Diego Conte Peralta | CFX Artist**

* * *

# **Could you tell us a bit about yourself?**

Hi! My name is Diego Conte, and I'm a CFX artist and 3D generalist working from Madrid, Spain. Because of my interest in computer graphics, I always wanted to work on the entertainment industry, which I'm happy to have been doing for the last 8 years. 

# **Which projects would you like to showcase today?**

I would say the most relevant projects are to this day all the short films I worked on for the incredible Spanish director Alberto Mielgo, including “The Witness” for Love Death and Robots and “The Windshield Wiper” (Academy award winner for best animated short film). His vision is still inspiring me today to keep pushing the boundaries of what cloth simulations can achieve in animation, and the part they can play as storytelling devices.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/20c207c8a2eb41dfbdbcd9a2c45bbcd7WD.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/97792d014ee84ba5a2ab4bdd330c083fWD_BTS02.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/2c9fbab6e7314b259212808a880d0506WD_BTS01.png)

# **What led you to choose Marvelous Designer, and how did it support your artistic vision?**

I came upon Marvelous Designer back in 2018 through my mentor at the time, Ash Thorp, who was using it in all sorts of fun and experimental ways for Motion Graphics. I picked it up, and was hooked from the start by the interactive and real time nature of the software. There is nothing like it really, the way you are directly interacting with the garments makes you forget at times that you are in front of a computer. How it supports my artistic vision is actually very tied to this interactive and realistic nature of the software. The fact that you are manipulating cloth as a tailor would do in real life means there is an added layer of naturalism to the results that can not really be achieved in any other software. And the interactivity means that there are also lots of possibilities for artistic expression that are just not easily available in traditional simulation tools.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/c77c918657544ff99e21f9be2b00c498sup.png)

# **Can you briefly walk us through the different tools you incorporate in your workflow?**

It has evolved quite a bit through the years! The main two areas of Marvelous I'm most familiar with are the pattern-making tools and simulation. I kept things fairly simple on the pattern making front on the first projects, and even now I keep things to just a few tools: drawing, sewing, tacks, pins, and sometimes creative use of internal lines to fold or art direct the patterns better.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/18d38e08f0da448e84dd7aeb5df1405cWSW_03.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/10bdf156fe6c4c67b5e9ef38d86f78e8WSW_02.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/b1dea4fd664446e78101abee204e8cafWTN_01.png)

# **What would you consider your most standout project where Marvelous Designer played a key role?**

I think "The Witness" is still the most iconic project I've worked on. The patterns for all garments had been created by Paloma Alperi by the time I arrived at the project, and so my task was to see if we could get something better from Marvelous Designer than the results they were getting simulating in Maya. The tests were very successful, so much so that, after I designed a custom workflow to implement Marvelous with the rest of the tools in the pipeline, we ended up simulating all garments for the show with Marvelous only, and I was lucky to supervise the cloth simulation team. I believe at the time it was the biggest production using Marvelous for all CFX shots, and its is probably still in the top of that list.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/6b2a4f56478f4ac89d6a9a619d46529aWTN_BTS01.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/3425c7f4db2f4003a5c774cc98defd05Thumbnail_02.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/251711ecb93a4177816205c7bb3b232eWTN_03.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/c37b9dce44ab4b15ab86e4683eaff808WTN_02.png)

# **Are there any upcoming projects where you plan to use Marvelous Designer?**

Of course! I will always advocate for integrating Marvelous Designer in any pipeline, big or small. Big projects require automation, but even when using other tools for simulation I believe the quality will always be higher when simulating a Marvelous designer garment compared to a traditional poly-modeling one. And for small projects, if it's possible to simulate in Marvelous designer, I'll always push for that first, as it is the most direct way to move forward

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/b4eb9b3dacd64e8f813066bd429715e5WSW_04.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/af515205b1364721a57fe68eaeb4e787/images/6ea2e7c265284b5e9331ba261ba0c401WSW_BTS01.png)

# **What advice would you offer to other artists utilizing Marvelous Designer for CFX work?**

I have three important pieces of advice.

For artists starting out, thorough research is crucial. Even if you feel well-prepared with reference materials (patterns, drawings, photographs), consider pushing your research further by reading pattern and fashion books, and any other material you can get your hands on.

For those familiar with the software, continue learning and thinking creatively. Marvelous offers numerous techniques and tools, so explore how they can work together. For example, you can use tacks, and you can use pins, but you would be amazed at what can be done when combining the two.

And finally, for professionals, while traditional studio pipelines seem to be set in stone (for good reason), it's important to reconsider how Marvelous could fit into your workflow. Don't be afraid to challenge established methods; this software operates on different paradigms that can lead to innovative solutions. And the overall pipeline will be better for it.

# **How would you sum up your overall experience with Marvelous Designer?**

There is always a thought that its repeated whenever I show anybody a behind the scenes of how Marvelous works, usually along the lines of "well, that looks like fun". And indeed, it is a lot of fun. And turns out you can be quite productive and get really good results when you have fun (or maybe because you are having fun!), which is why I keep going back to this software I love so much.

content:
## _Discover how Henri Gatard (@hgat_art ) brought history to life in 3D with Marvelous Designer—creating cinematic, stylized characters in Victorian and Napoleonic attire._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/11ad8cfde22a4870809a48912fab272f%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B51.png)

# **Interview with Henri Gatard |**[**Character Art Direction**](https://www.instagram.com/hgat_art)**| 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

I'm Henri Gatard, 23, Character Surfacing Artist at Gaumont in Paris and previously at Mathematic Studios. I love creating characters for animation, from the 2D concept to the final cinematic image, through all the stages of creation. I love creating characters from different eras, so I can tell different stories and achieve a unique look for animated characters. For my final images, I really try not to create characters that simply remain in a T pose in a lookdev. I always pose them to get a cinematic shot, and bring them to life as they might look in a movie. If you want to know more, you can find it all on [**my Instagram**](https://www.instagram.com/hgat_art/).

# **Tell us about your project. What inspired it, and what are its main themes?**

My project is my participation in the Rookies Award 2024 where I created 5 stylized characters and two of them have clothes made with Marvelous Designer. For these two characters, the Victorian soldier and the Napoleonic soldier, I really wanted to push my character skills and create stylized characters with historically accurate clothing and achieve a cinematic look with them. [**Link to my projects**](https://www.therookies.co/entries/30202)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/2ab77b0c529249f9922ffe53a3f0307a%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B53.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/8f230f9f5c3b445a84d9ce132bf09bb6%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B513.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/cd7ca91153f84b1a8f21f8d77d7b048c%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B514.png)

# **Why did you choose to use Marvelous Designer for this project? How did it help you achieve your art direction?**  

I chose Marvelous Designer because it was the best software for creating accurate garments based on how they are made in real life. I had a lot of garment models and historical references, and withMarvelous I was able to be very efficient because the software is based on how a garment is made in real life. Marvelous Designer was therefore the only possible choice for being able to create garments quickly with precise folds compared to sculpting everything in ZBrush.

# **Could you briefly walk us through the different tools and software used in your workflow?**  

Character Modeling/Blocking : ZBrush, Maya

Cloth Modeling/Retopology : Marvelous Designer, Maya

Texturing : Substance Painter/Designer

Rigging : Maya, Advanced Skeleton

Lighting/Rendering : Maya, Redshift

Compositing : Photoshop and Nuke

# **Could you explain the costume concepts of your characters in more detail? What specific elements did you focus on while designing the costumes in Marvelous Designer?**

For my character Victorian, this was my first Marvelous experiment in dressing a full-fledged character, so I kept it pretty simple. I made a long Victorian leech coat and classic pants. I wanted his outfit to be a bit classy but also marked by time. Here are my references.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/fad6989a3bae4027873414803af5a063henri%20.png)

Sketches and First Concept

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/3f7f080bf74647de8df84d8425d1bc18%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B57.png)

In Marvelous Designer, I tried to focus on the overall shape and pattern, for this character I just had three different garments because I wanted to keep it simple for the first time in Marvelous Designer. So I tried to get something that looked good without being complex.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/0608292b507348529ae13673d93c10e2%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B58.png)

For the Napoleonic soldier, I tried to go further in the design and complexity of the fabric. So I chose to make a Polish lancer from the Imperial Guard, these soldiers had a rather unique uniform with lots of detail and special stitching. I spent a lot of time finding historical references and archives.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/da06813a8f3f482da0fc37e9d519bb88henri%202.png)

For this one, I really concentrated on understanding the costume, there were lots of different parts and specific sewing with each part so it was quite difficult at first to really understand and place everything there was to do.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/d50fd6294ed44bcd8e717289f3118182Marvelouspatternnapoleonic.jpg)

# **What were the main challenges you faced while working on this project, particularly with the costume design?**  

These were my first projects with Marvelous Designer, so my main challenge was to understand the patterns and sewing, and reflect this in the simulations. Trying to reproduce the historical costume was also a challenge, especially for the Napoleonic, which has many different pieces.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/e7f1434cc2f14b48835a9817f852028c%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B519.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/a6d31335b97e4e8582609b5cfb949e4b%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B520.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/ddb75af5713a48d09f0ce2e70d6b7240%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B510.png)

The retopology was quite a difficult part to keep the details of the different parts, I did the retopology in Maya (I just discovered that there is a retopology mode directly in Marvelous Designer). My modeling work consists of exporting the flat patterns and simulated fabric from Marvelous Designer and retopologizing the flat pattern and transferring the position attribute by UV from the simulated fabric to the flat retopologized. Then I merge the parts and start detailing them in Maya.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/b938251a5db74f11b918549d2f336850retopologycloth.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/5705657107c24cfbbfca5070a4be6c65%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B518.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/a96c81a8119541e9ae7c8ab62098082eclothworkflow_02.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/a8efb6404b49450e9227c07e35338572modelTOPOwireframe.jpg)

I used the same workflow for my Victorian character.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/f242a9ed2cfe43fdbccd1e4a9f6b4d3e%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B512.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/d5019c8a2c0a40ac96f92feb11cd6503%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B511.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/b237a72c0d014a419aaf22fd1a71eddcmodelTOPOwireframevic.jpg)

And the most interesting part was the texturing inside of Substance Painter, with the Marvelous Designer workflow it was easier because the UV are already done and are based on the different seams. So the textures react as they would in real life. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ea11111fc8bf42c4a5fe3e0a9bc32f28/images/7731658467754049983f287148186e34%E5%A3%AB%E5%85%B517.png)

# **What tips would you give other artists using Marvelous Designer for character design in animation?**

I'm fairly new to Marvelous Designer so I don't know if I can give advice to other users, but for new users don't be scared off by the software, just dive in it's an amazing tool, you'll really improve your character by having accurate and realistic clothing without the difficulty of creating accurate creases as you would have done by hand in Zbrush. And your texturing workflow will be improved too. And don't be afraid to create complex garments like a Napoleonic costume with Marvelous if you have good references, you can do things that look difficult very easily! 

# **How would you describe your overall experience using Marvelous Designer?**

The experience was really great for my first few projects in Marvelous Designer, I didn't really have any difficulties learning the software and everything went smoothly during the designs, even when I didn't know how to do certain things. I was really happy to have MD in my toolbox because it took my characters to another level with cool fabrics and now I can design more characters with complex clothes without restricting myself!

# **by  Henri Gatard**

title: Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe
content:
## _Explore the Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe, a game-ready 3D fashion creation designed with Marvelous Designer, blending precision and futuristic aesthetics._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/ce2621cd4e774107855c688bf69549a31-1.jpg)

# **Interview with  **[**Wallet**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/xDla8E)**  | Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe****  | ****3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hello everyone, I'm Wallet (我是你的小钱包呀！). I am a former senior 3D character artist at Activision Blizzard, having participated in projects like Destiny 2, Call of Duty 17, and Call of Duty 18, with 11 years of experience in realistic game development. I specialize in creating realistic character models and excel in modeling characters, hard surfaces, and clothing, particularly in detailing. Currently, I work at Tencent TiMi Studio, focusing on the creation of trendy clothing.

# **Tell us about the project - Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe**

**Production Opportunity  **

The Balenciaga X-Pander spring shoes were a game model created in collaboration with the official Balenciaga brand for our company's game project. I needed to achieve scanning-level precision for this model and completed the high-accuracy production in Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/57fa951b00054573b36c2c9c3e0d6a311-3.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/8922364f21d04709bd203973de50604d1-2.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/f0287b1cf47f42b0a73c754828dd704a1-4.png)

**Material Collection  **

In the process of creating realistic models, I typically started by gathering a large amount of relevant materials, such as details from various aspects of the shoes, showcases of the shoe's shape, and resources that clearly displayed the structural details. Good reference materials significantly enhanced my production efficiency.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/9f2d8363ad0546239201b52ad5dc2f3a2-1.png)

**Creation of Sole and Last  **

The approach to making shoes differed slightly from that of regular clothing. For typical clothing, I could start directly in Marvelous Designer, but for shoes, I first created the last and sole. The sole served to stabilize the base, while the last shaped the overall structure of the shoe. In ZBrush, I sculpted a simple last based on reference images.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/c79262cff43543b9a8ce7d64cda533012-2.png)

Next, I created the sole based on this last. The sole of this shoe was quite complex, so I used Plasticity for its creation. This software was the most convenient and suitable NURBS modeling tool for game modeling that I had used in recent years. Especially with the introduction of new CV modeling, it had become even easier to work with. I used an older version without CV modeling, relying on traditional curves and boolean operations for the modeling process. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/79cc6e2412c8470ba3da8538f80ba2ae4.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/6591d484c3b74f068beb87e2091982783.png)

After completing the sole, I extracted the surfaces from it to use as the base pattern for the subsequent Marvelous Designer work. This pattern played a stabilizing role in Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/c9ef3fcd691a46ed94c922f0c2dab2685.png)

Since the pattern obtained from Plasticity did not have UVs, I also unwrapped the UVs in a 3D software.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/28d92fb589784e1c9b1f49f19bd01f676.png)

After obtaining the UVs, I imported them into Marvelous Designer by converting them for clothing use.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/94230099b50f4db284b15d6db10b11a57.png)

By selecting the 2D pattern on the UV map, I converted the model into a pattern piece.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/24f22b80c76f44d7b815260069a909a68.png)

Next, I will create the upper of the shoe based on this sole.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/1544cfcc05e24eea9b05fba41cdbec0f9.png)

**Marvelous Designer Pattern Making**

**Creating the Shoe Upper****  **

Using the previously created sole pattern, I began to extend and create the entire shoe pattern. The mesh upper was the most important part, and I chose to sculpt this model in ZBrush. I sculpted a rough shoe based on references and then retopologized it. Following the same method used for the sole, I created the upper, ensuring proper UV mapping. After converting it for clothing use and importing it into Marvelous Designer, I obtained the initial shoe upper pattern. The initially imported pattern had many unnecessary points, which I cleaned up.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/f7f29ca3d4294efa82469150c4ca859510.png)

**Creating the Upper Assembly Pattern Pieces****  **

For the other pattern pieces on the shoe upper, I prefer to use draping techniques. In Marvelous Designer, I can create these draped patterns using line segments.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/54fcabc9493b442d8b27c0bb44ed5b5311.png)

This approach allowed me to quickly draw pattern pieces directly onto the shoe upper.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/90bf93e8fb634a5bb62244b9f7cdb68912.png)

I selected the editing line segments and right-clicked to convert them into internal shapes.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/f615fc05a16643b58b2c599b318a533413.png)

By following this method, I was able to create all the pattern pieces. After obtaining these internal shapes, I pressed the "I" key to outline them as pattern pieces, completing the assembly pieces on the shoe upper.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/6cf8ba6d9d084a9787e1ea839e673d2414.png)

There were many assembly pattern pieces on the shoe upper, so in the end, I obtained a complex internal shape. I retained these internal shapes, as they would serve as the sewing edges for the subsequent sewing patterns.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/dfe1e56451ca4fddbf5c86c69128ba8615.png)

**Sewing Patterns****  **

For the majority of shoes, we typically assume that the pattern pieces are completely symmetrical, which makes the process much easier. Therefore, I only needed to create the pattern pieces for one side, and during sewing, I also only had to sew one side.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/ff42fa54e0d74b14b44a805cae07985416.png)

There wasn't much to say about the sewing patterns. The only aspect that needed emphasis was the overlapping relationships between the pattern pieces. While this wasn't complex, the process could be a bit tedious to operate.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/f96e3650e7974032aeda172639237e4617.png)

There were many instances of such layered sewing in this shoe. While following the realistic method of layering and sewing each piece was a bit cumbersome, it allowed for a more delicate representation of authenticity.

Realistic modeling focuses on ensuring that the overall shape is correct and visually appealing while paying attention to the creation of minute details. Only by doing so can a true sense of texture be achieved in the final presentation.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/95f47761ac58468d8e4765ea4656bdea18.png)

**Creating the Shoelaces****  **

The shoelaces for this shoe are round, so I couldn't simply use a single pattern piece. Instead, I used a double-layered sewing technique, which resulted in a much more natural appearance.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/97933f470d344c6da154b3821ed9d1ef19.png)

I created a faux effect for the shoelaces passing through the holes. Of course, it was possible to follow the realistic method of threading them through, but that was a bit more complicated. Instead, I directly sewed the shoelaces to the edges of the holes.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/df452890e37f4303a7da4e7907e6d18820.png)

**Final Adjustments****  **

In this step, I made overall minor adjustments to areas that differed from the references, correcting any interlacing or distortion issues caused by the complex sewing.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/64866689c69248ef88764b26ddf16b8b9c90483f73bf4fa0af9dc6a9af07cb0f.jpg)

Final Presentation on Marvelous Designer

**Creating the Mesh Texture in Substance 3D Designer****  **

The mesh for this shoe was quite unique, and after searching through existing mesh textures, I found that none were suitable. Therefore, I decided to create the mesh texture using Substance 3D Designer. Compared to the complex patterns typically made in Substance 3D Designer, creating this mesh was relatively simple. I later obtained a displacement map, which I used in ZBrush to convert into a model.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/1e1ab73dea0e4a4aaa0cbe27020adbd024.jpg)

**Refinement in ZBrush**

The process in ZBrush was similar to my usual clothing handling. I first cleaned up the mesh, using the workflow diagram from my previous racing suit project as a reference.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/a1aa6ab5a4ef4c70b898a0053b8d237125.png)

After cleaning up the mesh, I proceeded with the normal refinement work, which included:

  1. Adding wrinkle variations that Marvelous Designer couldn't handle

  2. Enhancing fabric changes at the seams

  3. Introducing memory folds

  4. Refining the edges

  5. Adding texture details

  6. Creating simple textures in ZBrush


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/eb0c055b45b247c399055a5e818afd6026.png)

In ZBrush, I preferred to express all details through the model. For the shoe's detail creation, I divided the process into three layers:

  1. **Base Texture** : I selected base textures according to different materials.

  2. **Wear Effects** : Materials like leather and cotton are the most susceptible to showing wear. Leather develops cracks and wrinkles over time, while cotton forms memory folds.

  3. **Edge Details** : The front, back, and side of the leather exhibit three distinctly different textural states. The front is smooth due to processing and features the unique grain of the leather, while the side shows a cross-section, revealing the torn appearance of the leather. For the shoelaces, the front is woven, and the side shows the seams of the weaving. Addressing these details significantly enhances the overall realism.




**Final Rendering**

For the final rendering, I used Keyshot, primarily because it supports a very high polygon count. Renderers like Blender and Marmoset cannot handle high-resolution models, and I prefer not to create low-poly versions. Therefore, Keyshot was an excellent choice, and I also opted to create the materials directly within Keyshot.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/d714340faaec4448aeff52370348ba7a32.png)

**Summary**

The shoe creation process was quite intricate, especially in achieving the special interlacing design within the streamlined structure, which took considerable time while also ensuring the stability of the shoe shape. Additionally, the detail handling in ZBrush was time-consuming. In terms of Marvelous Designer, the requirements for pattern-making in shoe design were relatively lower, making the process simpler compared to clothing creation.

# **In your "Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe" project, you used Marvelous Designer for the initial pattern making. What made you choose Marvelous Designer for this process?**

The draping feature in Marvelous Designer is extremely convenient, allowing me to easily create the intricate pattern pieces on the shoe upper. Most importantly, it supports modifications at any time. While traditional methods can also quickly produce models, they are relatively cumbersome to modify, especially when dealing with complex patterns. Additionally, although the shoe's materials are stiff and less prone to wrinkles, the shoes made in Marvelous Designer may lack some realism. However, they still exhibit a certain degree of authenticity. The fabric simulation in Marvelous Designer can convey subtle realism, making it more natural than hand-sculpting.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

The entire process involved using Marvelous Designer for initial pattern-making, Substance 3D Designer for creating the shoe's mesh, Plasticity for the sole construction, ZBrush for detailing, and Keyshot for the final rendering.

# **Are there any areas/ideas you would like to utilize Marvelous Designer in your future project?**

Yes, I will continue to use Marvelous Designer in other game projects, as well as in my own design projects. I am currently working on a new tutorial case.

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

Marvelous Designer is essentially a garment design software, so to create reasonable and aesthetically pleasing clothing, users need to possess certain pattern-making skills and basic knowledge of garment construction. This will better assist them in achieving their desired design outcomes.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Among the various fabric simulation software and plugins I use, Marvelous Designer is irreplaceable. Although it may be slightly inconvenient compared to some emerging software or plugins in certain aspects, this does not detract from its outstanding and precise simulation results.

# **by  ****Wallet (我是你的小钱包呀！)**
