content:
## _Experience 3D digital fashion on Samsung's 8K display at ISE 2024! See Sangyeop's futuristic designs crafted with Marvelous Designer in a stunning showcase._

* * *

# **ISE 2024 Samsung - Retail display In Barcelona | Sangyeop Jeong | 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Could you briefly introduce yourself and share how you got started with 3D work?**

Hello, my name is Sangyeop Jeong, and I'm a 3D artist. I'm currently part of Rabbit Walks, based in Seoul. I first fell in love with 3D after watching The Lord of the Rings in theaters when I was in elementary school, and that's when I started dreaming of becoming a 3D artist. Since I started as a modeler, I mainly work on character and product modeling, look deb, and also work on scene work and motion graphics. I mainly work on commercials, games, and also active as a freelancer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/ada2f34b250f4dd794c3bf232664014f%E4%B8%89%E6%98%9F%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%B03.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/c79ec4dd503447cc9f3ef3e8f5ada53c%E4%B8%89%E6%98%9F%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%B02.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/a6d76c6120364f61bc024acdbd451618%E4%B8%89%E6%98%9F%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%B01.png)

# **I found your ISE 2024 Samsung - Retail display project really impressive. Could you explain the concept behind it? I’m also curious about where you drew inspiration from when developing the concept.**

The ISE 2024 Samsung-Retail display project was done by Rabbit Walks. We designed it to align with a brand store concept that blends a futuristic-tone space, digital model runway, and product display. We created a sleek, futuristic mood and matched the space with the products using neon lights and linear elements to enhance the futuristic vibe.

We gathered a lot of references from Behance, Pinterest, and Instagram. Since I've always been interested in fashion, I follow a lot of related accounts, which really helped in developing the concept. This was a team effort in both planning and execution, and as the lead artist, I taught team members Marvelous Designer and directed the project overall.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help with providing art direction?**

I first encountered Marvelous Designer about 10 years ago when I was learning 3D and creating clothes for characters. Ever since then, I've considered it the most intuitive and efficient tool for fashion and clothing work.

For this project, there were many types of clothing, and each scene had a different composition based on the screen it was displayed on. To speed up the workflow, we simplified some of the detailed parts, diverging from our usual pipeline.

**#General pipeline**

  * Clothing modeling / UV layout (Marvelous Designer, Maya) - Texturing (Substance Painter)

  * Character rigging, posing, animation (Cinema 4D, Maya, Mixamo)

  * Cloth simulation (Marvelous Designer)

  * After simulating the clothes, we separated patterns and parts, then baked them as Alembic files in Maya.

  * Simulation development in C4D, final look development and scene lighting using Octane Render (Cinema 4D)


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/60a52a6a2a734119b5323dda0cf32026ISE%202024_8K_Still%20%283%29.jpg)

**#Marvelous Designer workflow**

  * Normally, after modeling the clothes in Marvelous Designer, I would go through the retopology process in Maya. However, I skipped that step and instead added internal lines to each pattern directly in Marvelous Designer to preserve the unique shape of the patterns as much as possible.


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/65feabe05be84c9bbfa65cb6737d48f6%E4%B8%89%E6%98%9F%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%B04.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/3e4f27518b584d65a5a8fbc66120b6a0%E4%B8%89%E6%98%9F%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%B05.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/cb8e53248af74ba29eae1d81c4c4d06e%E4%B8%89%E6%98%9F%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%B06.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/7f21bd22537748d7902aaae07a21052b%E4%B8%89%E6%98%9F%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%B07.png)

  * In Maya, after separating the simulation data from Marvelous Designer and keeping the history intact, you can align the frame count, select each pattern, and bake them again as Alembic files. This allows for efficient data management. 


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/ddcbbf69f18b45de81f7ff9d30387984MarvelousDesignerInterview_3_3-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/09471f974d5f4904a01cf75063bd0037Marvelous%20Designer%20Interview_3%E1%84%87%E1%85%A5%E1%86%AB%20%E1%84%8C%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AF%E1%84%86%E1%85%AE%E1%86%AB%20%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%84%85%E1%85%AD_2-1.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/53b23ee382ce4bbfa9228d8b6a2b20a6Marvelous%20Designer%20Interview_3%E1%84%87%E1%85%A5%E1%86%AB%20%E1%84%8C%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AF%E1%84%86%E1%85%AE%E1%86%AB%20%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%84%85%E1%85%AD_2-2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/89a6d01ab78649be8164e9666911e600Marvelous%20Designer%20Interview_3%E1%84%87%E1%85%A5%E1%86%AB%20%E1%84%8C%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AF%E1%84%86%E1%85%AE%E1%86%AB%20%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%84%85%E1%85%AD_2-3.png)

  * When modeling in Marvelous Designer, it is important to create sturdy patterns from the start to ensure the clothes fit well during simulation without becoming loose. To achieve this, I often work with double-sided patterns and make good use of the Strengthen feature. While this makes the data heavier, it allows for more stable modeling and simulation results. 

  * For each animation, I placed pins in specific areas to shape the clothes as desired, and I adjusted the Physical Property values for each pattern according to the scene.


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/36e60dc02ea649f093fd683a0c03358cMarvelousDesignerInterview_3_4-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)

  * The simulation data from Marvelous Designer was further refined in Cinema 4D using the Cloth and Wind features, resulting in more detailed simulation outputs. (Work tip from artist Hyejin Jang)


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/9a7739cbcff1489dbcf673e5705d5cd0MarvelousDesignerInterview_3_5-1-2-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/d1693fed7fa44a5c998eaf2d16b63f85/images/52e3e5e0175242f388fa384b4ba2389bMarvelousDesignerInterview_3_5-2-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)

# **While working on the project, there must have been aspects you enjoyed and others that were challenging. What was the most enjoyable part of the process for you?**

I truly love working in 3D, so even though there are challenges with each project, I find every step enjoyable. However, I especially enjoy modeling, texturing, and look development. In this project, the most fun part was being able to create a variety of clothing. Not only clothing, but I also modeled props like shoes and hats using Marvelous Designer.

# **Then, what was the biggest challenge you faced while working on the project?**

As I mentioned earlier, this project had a lot of different types of clothing, and each scene varied based on the screen, which meant there was a huge amount of work to do. This was the most difficult and challenging part for both my team and me. However, because of this variety, I was able to feel engaged throughout the work, making it less tedious and allowing me to enjoy the process.

# **Finally, do you have any advice for those just starting in 3D art? It can be career advice or tips on mindset when creating artwork—anything is welcome.**

First and foremost, it is really important to be clear about why you chose 3D and to enjoy and love what you do. This industry is intense and rapidly changing, so you can't afford to stop working or studying, and there is a lot of pressure. However, if you stay focused and believe in yourself while putting in the effort, I believe good results will follow. I still have a lot to learn, so I keep these thoughts in mind as I work.

## _As an Environment Artist at OVFX Studios, Raghav brought breathtaking dome tents to life in his mentorship project at Think Tank Training Center._

* * *

# **Interview with Raghav Verma |**[**Swamp Haven**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/n0R1g6)**| 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hey! My name is Raghav Verma, I’m currently working as an Environment Artist at the OVFX Studios for an unannounced Netflix and Hulu title. What can I say, I love to create things! Be it environment, props, or procedural systems for environments! My focus remains on game art which uses real-time rendering pipeline using game engines like Unreal Engine to create beautiful environments. I'm also a ThinkTankTraining Centre Alumni, and I’m known for my popular game environment project named [**_Swamp Haven_**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/n0R1g6) which is my latest environment project.

# **Tell us about the project - Swamp Haven**

[** _Swamp Haven_**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/n0R1g6) is my mentorship project which was made as a part of my final term at my art school, i.e. Think Tank Training Centre. It was an ambitious project that I took the responsibility of to finish in 4 months of time. It focused on pushing my technical skills to make high quality game assets.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/83edc4f47c514b1eb442e678ab2db557%E6%B2%BC%E6%B3%BD%E5%9C%A3%E5%9C%B01.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/a719e6e00f204852be5be8df2cf44ef5MainShot.jpg)

# **You used Marvelous Designer for cloth simulation of the tents. Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer?**  

Marvelous Designer is the best go to software for making real-time cloth simulations, especially ones that require a lot of manual art direction. The availability of GPU driven simulation is a big help when it comes to creating cloth simulations in a tight schedule. However it also features CPU simulations for more accurate sims. SwampHaven had to be completed in 4 months, and I had tasks every single day which needed to be done quickly, especially the Dome Tents. The Tents were a reimagined version of the concept art that I followed. They had to make physical sense for which I designed some ideas with my mentor Declan Hart. Finally a dome tent with modular cloth parts was the idea we landed up on. Marvelous Designer helped a ton while making the cloth sims because of its wide variety of tools that helped in making the sims quick and simple.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/d3c53579e564440f80183d7e36b86666%E6%B2%BC%E6%B3%BD%E5%9C%A3%E5%9C%B01.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/4f16e0d47a844633a1ea8fd20cad7d172_C.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/0bd48bb1f0a34691add95ab23ada7663Tents_Unreal.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/6cb0cbef9d4e4d589f94321fa6fec7b0%E6%B2%BC%E6%B3%BD%E5%9C%A3%E5%9C%B03.png)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline to complete the tent creation?**  

For the most part, Pinning tools and Measure tools were the most important tools which were used for my Dme Tents. The ability to create attachment curves at a collision mesh using ‘Attach to Measure’ and ‘Surface Measure’ helped the cloth to stick to my meshes properly. Furthermore, the ability to add ‘Pressure’ to the geometry paired with availability of different types of cloth types also helped a ton in art directing the look of the cloth simulation.

Furthermore these tools used my Unreal Engine shader system which allowed me to control different types of control on the texture, like the color, dirt spread etc. as shown below. 

# **What tips do you have for other artists using Marvelous Designer for environment art for games?**

For the limited time that I have used Marvelous Designer, I’d say it’s a great tool for making quick static meshes that require drapery or any type of cloth sim. Compared to other softwares, the UI is easy enough to grasp and the ability to play around with the cloth while it’s simulating in real time allows for greater control in art directing any cloth mesh. I’d recommend artists to check out Marvelous Designer for generating quick and detailed cloth sims for their project because of its easy to learn pipeline.

# **Are there any areas/ideas you would like to utilize Marvelous Designer in your future project?**

For future I’d like to explore Marvelous Designer for animated cloth sims on an animated actor/avatar. I’ve seen some cool showcases of cloth sims on characters which look amazing. I’d love to try that out.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Overall, Marvelous Designer offers a robust set of tools for doing cloth simulation quickly and efficiently. It helps in art directing cloth in many ways that helps both environment and character artists and is an amazing go to tool for simulations!

# **_by  Raghav Verma_**
